title: Making Dinner
subtitle: Rice, chicken, and one thing Emma always forgets.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about cooking at home: the food, the steps and the kitchen words.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: Tonight it is my turn to cook. I am not a good cook, but I make three or four things well, and chicken with rice is one of them.
First I look in the refrigerator. I have chicken, rice, onions, and half a lemon. I do not have bread. I always forget the bread.
I put water in a pot for the rice. While the water gets hot, I cut the onions. My eyes hurt a little, but only for a minute.
I put oil in a pan and I cook the chicken. It takes about fifteen minutes. The kitchen smells very good.
“Yes. Put the plates on the table, please. And open the window — it's hot in here.”
We eat at half past seven. It is not a special dinner, but it is hot, we are hungry, and there is enough for tomorrow.

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.prompt: What does Emma say about her cooking?
options: She makes a few things well
items.explanation: “I make three or four things well.”
“I do not have bread. I always forget the bread.”

items.prompt: What does she do while the water gets hot?
items.explanation: “While the water gets hot, I cut the onions.”

items.prompt: What does Jack do to help?
options: He puts the plates on the table and opens the window
items.explanation: That is what Emma asks him to do.

items.prompt: Why is Emma happy with the dinner?
options: It is hot, they are hungry, and there is food for tomorrow

items.prompt: Ask for help with the table.

exercises.title: In the Kitchen
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with one word.

items.prompt: I keep the milk in the ___.
Put the water in a ___ and make it hot.
items.explanation: A pot is deep; a pan is wide and flat.

items.prompt: I ___ the onions with a knife.
items.explanation: To cut is to divide with a knife.
To smell is to have a smell.
Enough means as much as you need.
